A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGP-CDE research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on three-variable and ten-variable synthetic data, Syntren and Sachs, plus a DGP-CDE restart analysis.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and Syntren evaluations, including larger graphs, an additive-noise ablation and sample-size sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: v1 uses matrix-exponential acyclicity with augmented-Lagrangian optimization. v2 replaces this with a largest-eigenvalue constraint, power-iteration gradient approximation and an increasing linear penalty, substantially changing the optimization procedure. The GP-CDE representation and hyperparameter-based adjacency remain. Appendix I.1 also introduces the latent-free CGP ablation.

E1.justification: v2 removes Sachs and adds sparse/dense 20- and 50-variable ER/SF scenarios and Gaussian-process additive-noise datasets. Three-variable synthetic data and Syntren remain. The ten-variable ER/SF benchmark evaluation is replaced, although ten-variable ER graphs remain in v2 for hyperparameter tuning.

E2.justification: The corresponding three-variable and Syntren comparisons replace GraN-DAG and GraN-DAG++ with SDCD and DiBS. v2 additionally evaluates a uniform-random DAG baseline in Figure 1 and the restricted CGP comparator in Figure 4. NOTEARS, CAM, SCORE, NOGAM and the three-variable DGP-CDE comparison remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds normalization during synthetic data generation, beyond v1's final standardization. Reported CGP-CDE settings change from 128 to 256 examples per minibatch, 100 to 50 latent Monte Carlo samples, and 30,000 to 25,000 warm-up/cool-down iterations. NOTEARS switches from a fixed 0.3 threshold to binary-search thresholding. Appendix I.2 adds evaluation at 100, 500 and 1,000 samples.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix I adds a latent-variable ablation comparing CGP-CDE with CGP on additive and non-additive data, and a sample-size sensitivity study. These directly examine flexibility and data requirements. The DGP-CDE restart analysis is retained, while v1's Sachs PKA-to-ERK model-fit case study is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 introduces standard-error bars across five graphs. The existing restart analysis retains standard deviations over 50 restart-order permutations. Reported CGP-CDE optimization restart counts also change: three to two for the three-variable experiment and two-to-five to two for Syntren. These are changed restart budgets, not evidence of increased independent replication.

E6.justification: v2 adds larger-graph, ablation and sample-size results and updates the three-variable/Syntren comparisons. It removes the ten-variable benchmark results and Sachs Table 1, where CGP-CDE scored SHD 17, SID 59 and F1 0.48. New Figure 4 shows comparable CGP/CGP-CDE performance on additive-noise data and an advantage for CGP-CDE on non-additive data. Changed settings prevent a clean same-setting performance comparison between versions.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix A primarily discusses identifiability informally. v2 Section 3 and Appendix B add formal error and equivalence definitions, a lemma, theorems, a corollary and proofs concerning recovery across MECs and distinguishability within an MEC, with explicit consistency and prior-separability conditions. Appendix A.2 also introduces the spectral constraint and its gradient mathematics.

C1.justification: The continuous Bayesian MAP discovery contribution remains, but v2 adds an explicit theoretical contribution explaining multivariate distinguishability. Its introduction and conclusion strengthen competitive-feasibility claims to outperforming Bayesian and non-Bayesian alternatives across multiple settings. Explicit claims of demonstrated real-world dataset performance disappear with the Sachs evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications connecting estimated error to model misspecification through total variation, interprets the new ablation through Bayesian Occam's razor, and attributes DiBS's poor performance to Bayesian neural-network inference. Appendix I discusses sparse-graph and small-sample exceptions. The Sachs ground-truth uncertainty discussion and associated interpretation are removed.

D1.justification: v2 revises optimization, stopping and restart specifications, documents spectral-penalty tuning and new baseline implementations, and adds a code/data repository link and A100 hardware information. Reproducibility ambiguities remain: Appendices C.3 and C.6 describe penalty increments differently, and Algorithm 1 places score storage outside the restart loop despite the accompanying restart description.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the literature supporting its optimization and theoretical positioning, including NOBEARS/SDCD, Bayesian consistency and standardized structural causal models. It explicitly positions the nonparametric MEC result relative to earlier parametric results and the prior bivariate framework. This extends v1's research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction and Bayesian background are substantially rewritten around explicit research questions and expanded explanations. Causal-model and continuous-optimization background moves into Appendix A, a theory section enters the main text, and the experiments, conclusion and appendix organization are reworked. These are extensive narrative changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v1's combined four-row benchmark figure is reorganized into separate main-text displays. v2 adds multi-panel ablation and graph-regime figures plus a sample-size plot, while removing the Sachs illustration, Sachs results table and identifiability schematic. The encoder table and restart plot are retained and relocated; the optimization pseudocode is reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central flexibility claim through explicit theoretical conditions and proofs, a targeted CGP ablation, sample-size sensitivity tests and broader graph regimes. Generation-time normalization improves experimental controls, and code/data access instructions aid reproducibility. Removing Sachs weakens real-data validation, and optimization documentation contains inconsistencies, but these drawbacks are outweighed by the stronger justification and targeted empirical scrutiny.
